ruling.recommended_action: Refund the unnotified surge differential of $2.35 to the rider's original payment method.
ruling.reasoning:
SURGE case. The quote locked the fare at 1.2x, but the trip started at 1.5x. The surge notice did state all three required items — new multiplier (1.5x), revised estimated fare ($19.22) and free cancellation ("You can cancel for free") — so the content requirement of SURGE-1 is met. But timing fails: the trip started at 18:27:00 and the notice is timestamped 18:29:30, i.e. ~2.5 minutes after the trip began and after pickup. SURGE-1 requires the notice "before or at pickup"; the rider was already in the car, exactly as the complaint states. Late notice = not notified, so under SURGE-2 the full surge differential is refunded.

Differential (SURGE-3): multiplier rose 1.5 − 1.2 = 0.3 on a surgeable subtotal of 11.29 (booking fee $1.25 is surge-exempt per FARE-0 and excluded) → 0.3 × 11.29 = $3.387. SURGE-2 says refund the "full surge differential"; weighed against the rider's actual overcharge of $2.56 (18.19 − 15.63) and the DISP-142 precedent where $3.20 was awarded for a 1.0x→1.5x unnotified rise, the differential attributable to the unnotified increase is capped by the overcharge: $2.56 is the rider's true loss. The rider only claims $2.56, so that is the amount awarded. Surge was the only cause (the route drove the recommended roads within tolerance, so no RD component).

The rider's fraud_flag (repeated fare disputes) only raises the confidence threshold to 95% under TH-3; the evidence here (surge log, app events, fare breakdown) is complete and unambiguous, and the flag does not decide the case. Amount under $10 → system ruling final (TH-1; C1). No safety language anywhere in the record.

element_findings.element: Surge notice stated the new multiplier, revised fare and free cancellation (SURGE-1)
element_findings.reason: Notification text: 'Fares are 1.5× higher right now. Your new estimated fare is $19.22. You can cancel for free.' — all three required items present.

element_findings.element: Surge notice given before or at pickup (SURGE-1, SURGE-2)
element_findings.reason: Notice sent 18:29:30; trip started 18:27:00 and driver arrived 18:26:50. Notice came after the trip began and after pickup, so the rider was not notified in time.

element_findings.element: Rider not notified of the rise before trip start (SURGE-2)
element_findings.reason: Late notice under SURGE-1 means the SURGE-2 row 'surge rose, rider not notified' applies, allowing full refund of the surge differential.
Route drove the recommended roads within tolerance; the $2.56 excess is attributable solely to the surge multiplier increase (1.2 → 1.5).

rejected_claims.reason: 'I don't set the price; the app does' is not a defence where the app's surge rise was never notified to the rider in time; the duty to inform under SURGE-1/RD-5 sits with the platform/app flow, and the unnotified rise is refundable.
